questions.a: 'has' — the committee acts as one unit submitting one report. A wrong answer 'have' suggests the student pluralizes all collectives reflexively, or over-applies the member-acting rule without checking for the unit reading.
'is' — 'news' ends in -s but is singular by convention. A wrong answer 'are' is pure spelling-agreement — the terminal -s hijacked the student's grammar.

questions.q: 'A pair of scissors ___ (is/are) on the table.'
questions.a: 'is' — the head is 'pair', singular; 'scissors' alone would take 'are'. A wrong answer 'are' shows the student agreed with the salient noun rather than the head — same failure as the decoy-phrase node, different costume.

questions.q: Collective nouns (team, committee, jury, family) take singular when the group acts as one unit and plural when members act ______ — 'The jury has reached a verdict' vs 'The jury are divided'.

Fill in the blank: Collective nouns (team, committee, jury, family) take singular when the group acts as one unit and plural when members act ______ — 'The jury has reached a verdict' vs 'The jury are divided'.
Fill in the blank: Act it out: 'The class is quiet' — one silent blob = ______. 'The class are arguing among themselves' — members doing different things = plural.
What must you be able to do to master this topic?
questions.a: The student chooses singular vs plural for collectives by asking 'unit or members?', and correctly handles fixed-form nouns (news singular, scissors plural) plus 'a pair of' constructions.

questions.q: Fill in the blank: Act it out: 'The class is quiet' — one silent blob = singular. 'The class are arguing among ______' — members doing different things = plural.
